claude_take: What stands out across today's set is how much energy goes into guarding access rather than earning it. Reddit is walling off two decades of open browsing, Cinemark is refusing to screen a film rather than negotiate shorter theatrical windows, and Frasers is tightening its grip on Hugo Boss's leadership without ever winning the company outright -- three different institutions digging in on control instead of adapting to what's already changed around them. Meanwhile Maxon is quietly wiring AI agents directly into professional VFX tools with barely any friction, which suggests the fights people actually pick aren't about AI or disruption in the abstract, but about who gets to decide. And against all that boardroom maneuvering and awards-season pageantry, Congo's Ebola outbreak -- still growing after six months, largely off the front page -- is a reminder of how unevenly urgency gets distributed.
claude_take_title: The Fights Aren't About AI. They're About Control.

items.headline: Maxon Ships a Major Cinema 4D and Redshift Update, With AI Agents Wired Into the Pipeline
items.summary: Maxon's Fall 2026 release brings version 2027.0 across its creative suite: a new procedural scatter system and liquid-effects tools in Cinema 4D, faster scene updates and render-time fur in the Redshift renderer, a new UV editor in ZBrush, and support for the Model Context Protocol in its Autograph compositor, letting outside AI agents operate the tool directly. It's a sign that agentic AI is being built straight into professional VFX pipelines now, not just consumer creative apps.

items.headline: Cinemark's CEO Explains Why It Won't Play Netflix's IMAX-Only 'Cliff Booth'
items.summary: Weeks after Cinemark and Regal declined to screen Netflix's 'The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth' on their IMAX screens, leaving AMC as the film's main IMAX partner, Cinemark's CEO used an earnings call to explain the refusal directly: the film's two-week theatrical exclusivity before it hits Netflix on December 23 isn't, in his words, 'constructive' for the theatrical ecosystem. It's the clearest on-record statement yet of exhibitors drawing a hard line on how short a streaming-to-theatrical window they'll accept, rather than quietly passing on a title.

items.headline: European Film Awards Nominations Led by 'Fatherland' and 'La Bola Negra'
items.summary: The European Film Academy has unveiled nominations for the 39th European Film Awards, announced November 14 in Thessaloniki. Pawel Pawlikowski's 'Fatherland' leads the field with 11 nominations, followed closely by 'La Bola Negra' with 10, while Cristian Mungiu's Palme d'Or-winning 'Fjord' picked up five nods. Winners will be decided at a ceremony in Athens on January 16, 2027.

items.headline: Marrakech International Film Festival Wraps Its 23rd Edition
items.summary: The Marrakech International Film Festival closes its 23rd edition today, after opening with Jesse Eisenberg's 'The Debut' and screening 76 films from 39 countries under a jury led by Marion Cotillard. The festival remains one of the most closely watched stops on the international circuit outside Europe and North America, drawing major international stars to Morocco each year.

items.headline: Reddit Moves to End Two Decades of Open, Logged-Out Browsing
items.summary: Reddit CEO Steve Huffman has confirmed the company is shifting toward a primarily logged-in experience, restricting access to old.reddit.com and testing broader login requirements outside the US starting this quarter. The company frames the move around personalization, ad targeting, and blocking AI scrapers, though critics note that determined scrapers can simply register accounts and keep harvesting content. It would mark the end of one of the last major sites that let anyone browse freely without an account.

items.headline: DR Congo's Ebola Outbreak Tops 11,000 Cases, Still Not Under Control Six Months In
items.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, driven by the rare Bundibugyo strain with no approved vaccine, has passed 11,000 confirmed cases and roughly 5,500 deaths, with Africa CDC saying it remains 'not under control' more than six months after being declared. The outbreak has already spread to Uganda and Kenya, with isolated cases reaching Nigeria and Europe via medical evacuation, and health officials describe it as the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record.

items.headline: Hugo Boss Names Frasers Executive David Epstein as Next CEO
items.summary: Hugo Boss has named David Epstein, an executive from majority shareholder Frasers Group, as its next chief executive, succeeding longtime CEO Daniel Grieder effective January 1, 2027. The appointment comes after Frasers built a stake approaching 48% in the German fashion house following a takeover offer that fell short of full control, and signals the retail conglomerate tightening its grip on Hugo Boss's leadership even without having won it outright.

items.headline: Merleau-Ponty's Lived Body
items.summary: Maurice Merleau-Ponty argued that our primary relationship to the world isn't through detached thought but through a 'lived body' that already understands space, tools, and other people before we consciously reason about any of it. Perception, for him, isn't data processing; it's a bodily, pre-reflective grip on a situation, which is why a skilled typist's fingers 'know' the keyboard without her having to think about it. The idea still matters today, as debates about AI and embodiment ask whether an intelligence without a body can ever understand the world the way we do.
items.summary_fr: Maurice Merleau-Ponty soutient que notre rapport premier au monde ne passe pas par la pensée détachée, mais par un « corps propre » qui comprend déjà l'espace, les outils et les autres avant toute réflexion consciente. Pour lui, percevoir n'est pas traiter des données : c'est une prise corporelle et préréflexive sur une situation, comme les doigts d'une dactylo expérimentée qui « savent » le clavier sans qu'elle y pense. Cette idée reste précieuse aujourd'hui, alors que les débats sur l'IA et l'incarnation interrogent la capacité d'une intelligence sans corps à comprendre le monde comme nous le faisons.
